resources.string: Two-finger swipe up or down to change volume anywhere.

Gesture Volume watches for a two-finger swipe up or down anywhere on screen and changes your media volume. It only observes touch events — it never blocks your normal taps and swipes, and it never reads screen content.
Works in any app. Normal taps, scrolling and pinch-to-zoom are untouched.
Service on, but touch observation unavailable
Add the “Volume Control” widget to your home screen for plus, minus, mute and a tap slider.
Toggle greyed out or “Restricted setting”? Tap here

Android 13, 14 and 15 block sideloaded apps from turning on Accessibility until you allow it manually. This is a normal Android security step, not a problem with the app.

Do this:

1. Go to Settings ▸ Accessibility ▸ Gesture Volume and try to turn it on. You will see the “Restricted setting” message. Dismiss it — this step is required to reveal the option.

2. Go to Settings ▸ Apps ▸ See all apps ▸ Gesture Volume. You must reach it through this full list, not from Recents.

3. Tap the ⋮ menu at the top right and choose “Allow restricted settings”, then confirm with your PIN or fingerprint.

4. Return to Accessibility and turn Gesture Volume on.

If the ⋮ menu has no such option (common on Android 15, OxygenOS 15 and ColorOS 15), uninstall the app, then reinstall the APK using a session-based installer from the Play Store such as “Split APKs Installer (SAI)”. That registers the install properly and the restriction no longer applies.

On Samsung: turn off Settings ▸ Security and privacy ▸ Auto Blocker first.
